name: Mended Net Cord
description: A small coil of flax cord, already knotted once and still strong enough to close a torn fishing net.

name: Plain Water Jar
description: A sound clay jar with a rope handle, light enough for a traveler to carry back from the well.

name: Boatwright's Adze
description: A compact iron-edged adze whose worn olive-wood handle fits the empty place in the boat-yard basket.

name: Road Bread
description: A round barley loaf wrapped in linen, enough to divide among several tired walkers at evening.

name: Watch Lamp Oil
description: A thumb-stoppered flask of ordinary olive oil, kept for a lamp that must remain lit through the night.

name: Pearl of Great Price
description: A luminous pearl carried by a traveling storyteller when speaking of a merchant's single incomparable find.

name: Lost Silver Coin
description: A small silver drachma used when telling of a house swept from corner to corner for one missing coin.

name: Mustard Seed Pouch
description: A thumb-sized cloth pouch holding seeds small enough to vanish in a palm and numerous enough to begin a thicket.

name: Waiting Wedding Lamp
description: A plain clay lamp kept trimmed for a wedding procession whose hour is known only when the street begins to stir.

name: Samaritan Oil and Linen
description: A travel flask and folded strip of clean linen for tending a stranger found hurt beside the road.
